title: Chocolate Pancakes with Chocolate Sauce
changes_from_base: Cocoa and an optional pinch of espresso go into a milk batter, the pancakes are small and thin, and a quick chocolate sauce replaces the maple syrup.
summary: Dark, rich chocolate pancakes—tender and not too sweet—with a silky chocolate sauce that flows warm and luxurious over the top.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan and to serve
fine instant espresso powder (optional, up to 1 tsp)

steps.title: Sift dry
steps.text: Sift 170 g plain flour, 32 g cocoa powder (natural, not Dutch-processed), 75 g caster sugar, 1½ tsp baking powder, ¾ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp bicarbonate of soda into a large bowl.

steps.title: Mix wet
steps.text: Whisk 2 large eggs, 180 ml whole milk, 42 g unsalted butter (melted) and ½ tsp instant espresso powder (optional, up to 1 tsp), pour into the dry mix and stir gently until just moistened (lumps remain; do not overmix).

steps.title: Butter pan
steps.text: Very lightly butter a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drop 2 heaped tbsp batter per pancake and spread to 8-9 cm (2.5-4 cm apart). Cook until the base is set, edges start to set and tiny bubbles form (about 1 min); flip with a lightly greased spatula and cook about 1 min more. Adjust heat to stop them over-browning; wipe the pan and butter it again between batches; keep warm under foil or in a 150 °C oven.

steps.title: Make sauce
steps.text: Heat 120 ml whole milk to a bare simmer over medium heat, add 142 g semi-sweet chocolate (finely chopped), take off the heat and whisk smooth; whisk in 1 tsp vanilla and serve straight away over the pancakes.

tips: A touch of instant espresso powder deepens the chocolate flavour without making the pancakes taste of coffee; it is entirely optional.
Natural cocoa powder (not Dutch-processed) gives a sharper, truer chocolate flavour; Dutch-processed is darker but slightly more mellow.
The sauce must be poured over the pancakes straight away whilst it is glossy and warm; if it cools and thickens, gently reheat it.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
